flows.narrative: The week through 19 Aug showed a decisive rotation into safe-haven/defensive assets: money-market/cash funds drew the largest inflow ($25.4bn), bonds $23.8bn, and gold $6.3bn — its biggest weekly inflow since January 2026 — as BofA's Michael Hartnett reiterated a 'long gold, short USD' stance. Equities still drew a net $16.1bn but this was a slowdown versus prior weeks, consistent with the tech-led deleveraging that hit semis hardest in the Aug 19 rout. Nothing in this release has changed since the weekend; the next print (Fri 28 Aug) will be the first to capture this week's Iran-sanctions rollout, Nvidia earnings and Jackson Hole. On the US-specific side, a direct ICI fetch this run confirms the latest weekly release (published 19 Aug, week ended 12 Aug) showed long-term fund flows of -$16.82bn (equity -$20.89bn: domestic -$17.18bn, world -$3.71bn; hybrid -$1.09bn; bond +$5.16bn: taxable +$3.62bn, muni +$1.54bn) — the week-ending-19-Aug release is not yet posted, as expected (~26 Aug). Vanda/JPM retail-flow commentary (proxy, not an official print) describes retail turnover near record highs (99.7th percentile) but net buying at its weakest pace since the COVID era.
